requiredBeforeFiling.why: the platform holds no value for this and the participant supplies it before filing: the case name exactly as it appears on your court paperwork — in a criminal case that is usually the State of Alaska against your name
requiredBeforeFiling.participantMustSupply: the case name exactly as it appears on your court paperwork — in a criminal case that is usually the State of Alaska against your name

requiredBeforeFiling.disclosureLabel: Ground 10 — the specific rule or statute number
requiredBeforeFiling.why: the platform holds no value for this and the participant supplies it before filing: the specific Alaska statute or court rule number that takes your case off the public index, if you ticked ground 10
requiredBeforeFiling.participantMustSupply: the specific Alaska statute or court rule number that takes your case off the public index, if you ticked ground 10

participantElections.label: Ground 1 — 60 days have passed since acquittal or dismissal (selection)
participantElections.why: tick this if you were acquitted of all charges, or all charges were dismissed and the dismissal was not part of a plea agreement in another criminal case, or a combination of the two — and 60 days have passed

participantElections.label: Ground 2 — a criminal case dismissed for one of the two reasons below (selection)
participantElections.why: tick this heading if one of the two reasons printed under it is why your case was dismissed

participantElections.label: Ground 2 — a judicial officer found no probable cause (selection)
participantElections.why: tick this if a judicial officer found no probable cause under Criminal Rule 4(a)(1) or 5(d)

participantElections.label: Ground 2 — the defendant was a minor wrongly charged in adult court (selection)
participantElections.why: tick this if the defendant was a minor and was wrongly charged in adult court with an offence within the jurisdiction for delinquency proceedings under AS 47.12.020

participantElections.label: Ground 3 — a criminal or minor offence case dismissed for one of the two reasons below (selection)
participantElections.why: tick this heading if one of the two reasons printed under it is why your case was dismissed

participantElections.label: Ground 3 — the prosecutor decided not to file a charging document (selection)
participantElections.why: tick this if the prosecutor decided not to file a charging document

participantElections.label: Ground 3 — there was an identity error (selection)
participantElections.why: tick this if there was an identity error under Criminal Rule 43(d) or Minor Offense Rule 11(c)

participantElections.label: Ground 4 — a suspended imposition of sentence, completed, with all other charges resolved (selection)
participantElections.why: tick this if you received a suspended imposition of sentence, completed the terms of the sentence, and were acquitted of — or had dismissed or set aside — all other charges in the same case. The form tells you to attach proof of the SIS and any order setting aside

participantElections.label: Ground 5 — all charges were underage alcohol offences (selection)
participantElections.why: tick this if every charge was one of the underage alcohol offences the form lists — AS 04.16.049, AS 04.16.050, AS 04.16.060(g), AS 28.35.280, AS 28.35.285 or AS 28.35.290 — or an equivalent municipal ordinance

participantElections.label: Ground 6 — a conviction for possessing less than one ounce of marijuana at 21 or older (selection)
participantElections.why: tick this if you were convicted of possessing less than one ounce of marijuana, were at least 21 at the time of the offence, and were not convicted of any other criminal charge in the same case

participantElections.label: Ground 7 — a closed protective order case in which no protective order was ever issued (selection)
participantElections.why: tick this if the protective order case is closed and no protective order was issued at any time in it

participantElections.label: Ground 8 — a protective order issued by another US court or tribunal (selection)
participantElections.why: tick this if the protective order was issued by a US federal court, another state or territorial court, a tribal court in the US, or a US military tribunal

participantElections.label: Ground 9 — already confidential or sealed by judicial order under Admin. Rule 37.6 (selection)
participantElections.why: tick this if a judge has already made the case confidential or sealed under Administrative Rule 37.6. The form tells you to attach a copy of that order

participantElections.label: Ground 10 — otherwise subject to removal by Alaska statute or court rule (selection)
participantElections.why: tick this if some other Alaska statute or court rule takes the case off the public index, and write the rule or statute number on the line below

protectedBlanks.label: Date of signature
protectedBlanks.why: you date it when you sign it; a date written in advance would be false
